summary: APM feed s107_single is degraded due to packet loss: 2.3% of TCP packets (57/2513) show missing data, exceeding 1% threshold. All other checks (duplicates, one-way, truncation, tunnels, VLAN, encryption, oversize, tool overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Visibility fabric is dropping packets under load - TCP sequence gaps/retransmission gaps indicate ~2.3% loss. With tool overload healthy and no truncation/oversize, loss is occurring upstream of the tool at the SPAN/TAP or packet broker ingress/egress buffers due to microbursts or sustained oversubscription/policing, not at the APM itself.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM requires both directions for transaction correlation. Missing segments cause incomplete flows, inaccurate latency/response-time calculations, false retransmission/timeout alerts, and missed or broken traces, reducing APM detection coverage and service-map accuracy.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute the feed across multiple 10G APM tool ports or broker egress groups with 5-tuple hashing to eliminate buffer drops and microburst loss while preserving both directions of each flow to the same tool instance.
